objects.why_kids_care: a chance to win a prize
objects.notes: Renamed from 'fair game' (an idiom that reads oddly in 'Maya has 3 fair games'). Ring toss, balloon pop, duck pond. Price is one play; count_one_kid is plays in one visit; count_group is booths on the midway.

Trips of 60-500 miles at about 60 miles an hour, with a stop every 2 hours. count_one_kid is trips in a year.
count_one_kid is stops on one trip. Stops add minutes to the arrival time.

objects.why_kids_care: little circles you count on each slice
objects.notes: A 6 oz package holds about 50 slices; about 5-8 per pizza slice, 40-60 per large pizza; equal sharing across slices.

objects.why_kids_care: snaps along the lines into halves and quarters
objects.notes: Full sheet is scored into 2 halves and 4 quarters; ideal for early fractions. A box holds about 24-27 full sheets in 3 sleeves.

settings: at halftime of a soccer game
objects.why_kids_care: peels into slices to share at halftime
objects.notes: About 10 segments each; 3-4 lb bag holds 8-10 oranges; distinct from the existing 'clementine' by size and segment count.

objects.why_kids_care: on a stick and dipped in ketchup
objects.notes: Frozen ones about $1 each (box of 8 for $7); fair or ballpark ones $5-7.

objects.why_kids_care: how many for a whole pile of fries
objects.notes: Each packet about 9 mL; good for 'how many packets fill a small cup' capacity questions.

objects.why_kids_care: the best part of school lunch
objects.notes: Half-pint school carton, 8 fl oz (about 240 mL); chocolate vs. white milk is a classic class survey.
Each needs 2 graham squares (half a sheet), 1 marshmallow, and part of a chocolate bar; about 45 g total; great 'how many can we make' multiplication.

objects.why_kids_care: you get to write on the board
objects.notes: Packs of 4, 8, or 12 colors.

settings: on a ring in a backpack
objects.why_kids_care: flip fast and beat your record
objects.notes: 3x5 inch cards; cards answered right vs. wrong makes data; use the pack price for money problems, not the per-card price.

objects.why_kids_care: five sections and the biggest one is for pizza
objects.notes: Rectangle with 5 or 6 compartments of different sizes; stacks of trays for skip counting.

objects.why_kids_care: the ones with cartoons make a scrape feel better
objects.notes: Renamed from 'adhesive bandage': 'adhesive' is not a K-1 reading word. Generic name for the sticky strip kind; boxes of 20-30.

objects.why_kids_care: punching in the number and hearing it drop
objects.notes: Prices like $1.25 or $1.75 make natural coin and change problems.

objects.why_kids_care: picking books with your own money at the fair
objects.notes: Kids arrive with $10-20; paperbacks $5-10 and hardcovers up to $15; prices like $5.99 and $7.99 make budgeting problems for grades 2-5; keep K-1 to whole-dollar counting.
Free-throw line is 15 ft (457 cm) from the backboard; made out of attempted gives fractions.

objects.why_kids_care: the ball flies over the fence
objects.notes: Youth fences about 200 ft (60 m); a home run is 4 bases at 60 ft each for kids' fields.

settings: at the end of the lane
objects.why_kids_care: ten in a triangle, knock them all down
objects.notes: Set of 10 in rows of 1, 2, 3, 4; regulation pin 15 in tall, about 3.5 lb; knocked down vs. standing is a perfect number bond to 10.

objects.why_kids_care: the kids you sit with every day
objects.notes: Class sizes 18-30; groups of 4 or 5 at tables for division.
Equal-sharing problems (cookies among friends) are the canonical use.
Teams of 5 (basketball), 6 (volleyball), 9 (baseball), 11 (soccer); 'split 24 kids into teams of 6'.

objects.why_kids_care: squeaks when it hears the veggie bag
objects.notes: Very common class pet; often kept in pairs; eats 1 cup of veggies a day.
Humpback about 15 m, blue whale up to 30 m; weight left null because grams are unusable at that scale.

objects.why_kids_care: eight of them and Earth is one
objects.notes: 8 planets in order from the sun; big-number comparisons for grades 4-5 (moons: Earth 1, Mars 2, Jupiter 95).

objects.why_kids_care: no school and sledding all day
objects.notes: Snow days per winter by region; also snowfall in inches or cm for measurement.
Boxes of 32 cards; one per classmate plus leftovers is a classic subtraction problem.

objects.why_kids_care: becoming a dragon for a day
objects.notes: Dress-up and October costume parades; class survey of costume types; no holiday named.

objects.why_kids_care: break it open and candy rains down
objects.notes: Pairs with existing 'pinata-candy'; filled weight 0.5-2 kg. Wording softened from 'whack it'.

settings: on a bike in the driveway
objects.notes: Always come in pairs; bike with training wheels has 4 wheels for counting. Narrowed to K-1: grade 2-3 kids have mostly outgrown them. Price and pack removed: adult purchase.

objects.why_kids_care: learning to tie the bunny ears
objects.notes: Kid laces 27-45 inches (70-115 cm); sold in pairs for $3-6; fun colored laces are a kid purchase.

settings: on the laptop cart at school
objects.why_kids_care: the screen tilts and the games load
objects.notes: School-issued laptops; screen is an 11-14 inch rectangle; open lid angle around 90-120 degrees. Price nulled: school or adult purchase.
